commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[ci] Bound Iris jobs launched by GitHub Actions (#9285)

GitHub Actions submissions to standing Iris controllers now receive
server-side execution deadlines. Six canary launchers and each weekly
storage-report stage expire after six hours. The shared CoreWeave
integration parent expires after 30 minutes, with Fray carrying that
deadline to Iris.

GitHub runner and monitor timeouts cannot terminate an Iris job after
the runner disappears. These server deadlines bound the remaining work
even when workflow cancellation skips cleanup.

The audit covered direct workflow CLI submissions, the Python storage
submitter, the shared CoreWeave integration workflow, and the hero
completion reconciler, which already had four-hour execution and 24-hour
scheduling deadlines. The other Iris integration workflow uses a local
ephemeral cluster that is torn down with its runner.

Incident: [CI jobs ran without server
deadlines](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/485)

---------

Co-authored-by: rjpower <rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: yonromai
commits.message:
Reduce Finelog cost for inference dashboards (#8930)

Fetch each inference telemetry series once in the Grafana bridge and
share the projected result across the overview and diagnostics pages.
This reduces Finelog query work from one scan per panel to one selector
scan and one bounded telemetry scan. The rebased dashboards retain
#9269's identity filter, which offers only runs that reported
`num_requests_running`.

For `/held/serve-grug-20260919-playground-weaver-r10` from 2026-09-19
15:07:57 to 18:07:57 UTC, the dashboard on main at `d2d97e8` issued 84
scans while loading the overview alone, and all ten panels exceeded the
10.21-second deadline. This branch issued two scans: the selector
returned in 0.72 seconds and the compact telemetry fetch returned in
0.29 seconds. The cold overview completed in 1.19 seconds; all ten
overview and 17 diagnostics panel requests returned successfully, and
warm page switches issued no new scans.

The shared projection preserves output-length buckets, the fraction of
engine finishes caused by the length limit, and mean inter-token latency
(ITL) per engine. Both pages open on five minutes and refresh every two
minutes; historical ranges remain selectable. Fetches are capped at one
million samples and 50,000 series, while local calculations use one
thread, a 512 MB managed-memory limit, and no disk spill. Dense ranges
that exceed these limits return an explicit error. Runs that did not
export native ITL leave that metric unavailable instead of estimating
it, so [MarinSkyRL PR
#515](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/515) affects
future telemetry but is not a merge prerequisite.

Part of #8929.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[data] Route TaskTrove MCQA for RL and SFT (#9264)

TaskTrove's cleaned release retained 611,698 MCQA tasks even though most
are better suited to supervised fine-tuning or are unusable. This change
adds a conservative routing pass and integrates its decisions into the
release pipeline.

The reusable routing `ArtifactStep` submits recoverable GLM-5.3 batches,
validates a forced tool response locally, and combines worker shards
into complete task-level `decisions.jsonl` and `route-mappings.jsonl`
artifacts. The completed artifact contains 603,290 mappings: 23,860 RL,
458,562 SFT, and 120,868 garbage. It is stored at
`s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/tasktrove/mcqa-routing/2026.09.18.1`.

The cleaner loads the canonical mapping JSONL once and applies a direct
map-side lookup by task ID. MCQA tasks routed to RL remain in the main
Harbor corpus and are also written to the route-specific RL split. SFT
candidates retain their task and solution payloads in a separate
Parquet. Garbage rows and MCQA rows absent from the mapping fail closed
without retained payloads. Non-MCQA rows are unchanged.

The release keeps the existing consumer contract through
`tasks/part-00000.parquet`, which remains the full RL-compatible corpus
with its prior schema. Existing `TaskTroveDataSource` users therefore
continue to read `tasks/` without changes. The new `rl/` and `sft/`
paths contain only MCQA rows assigned to those routes.

The `2026.09.18.3` release is stored at
`s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/tasktrove/clean/2026.09.18.3` and
contains:

- `tasks/part-00000.parquet`: 861,848 retained Harbor tasks using the
previous schema
- `rl/part-00000.parquet`: 23,860 MCQA tasks routed to RL, with routing
provenance
- `sft/part-00000.parquet`: 458,562 MCQA SFT candidates with routing
provenance and Harbor payloads
- `ledger.parquet`: rejected, garbage, and 8,408 fail-closed unmapped
MCQA rows
- `manifest.json` and `report.md`: route and release accounting

The SFT split preserves routed Harbor tasks for downstream single-turn
conversion; it does not perform that conversion in this release.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[finelog] Regenerate schema-derived table spec fields (#9272)

Regenerate schema-derived source-layout and artifact-policy fields from
the new logical schema when a managed registration updates an
object-backed table. Copying these fields from the active specification
retained values derived from the old schema. A production-catalog shadow
registration then rejected the telemetry table specification before the
session-discovery artifacts from #9269 could activate.

Preserve explicitly configured layout settings. Physical layout changes
continue through the existing migration lifecycle, while metadata-only
index and projection changes activate without rewriting stored rows.

---------

Co-authored-by: rjpower <rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: yonromai
commits.message:
[dependencies] Align TPU vLLM source at 70ea9ae8 (#9270)

Move Marin's TPU serving pin from vLLM `4c1c798a` to `70ea9ae8`, paired
with the unchanged tpu-inference source `29548fba`. This aligns the TPU
lane
with the vLLM source used by MarinSkyRL. Marin's GPU and MarinSkyRL pins
stay
unchanged, and no vLLM or tpu-inference source patch is required.

Record exact-source alignment as a preference when both device gates
pass.
GPU and TPU keep separate wheels, dependency environments, manifests,
gates,
promotion inputs, and release cadences. Compatibility or qualification
can
justify temporary source skew; record the reason and prefer a later
qualified
common commit without delaying either lane.

The exact Python 3.12 pair clean-installed; 44 checks covering the
paired
GrugMoE, model-loader, and nightly paths passed before candidate
publication.
The public candidate

[`marin-vllm-tpu-candidate-70ea9ae8f260-29548fbab663-cf8f3a6eb7e8-b5f5e06166f4`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/releases/tag/marin-vllm-tpu-candidate-70ea9ae8f260-29548fbab663-cf8f3a6eb7e8-b5f5e06166f4)
then passed the first and only physical run on one production-priority
`v6e-8`
in `us-east5`: Qwen3-0.6B started at tensor parallel size 8 and answered
all
four chat prompts with HTTP 200. [Qualification

35405315448](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/actions/runs/35405315448)
retains the validation record through `2026-10-03T00:12:21Z`.

Both source commits are already on their protected `main` branches.
Merge this
Marin PR first. Before the validation record expires, and after
confirming
vLLM `main` still contains the qualification-reuse path, a human can
promote
the same bytes with:

```sh
gh workflow run marin-gpu-release.yaml \
  --repo marin-community/vllm --ref main \
  -f lane=tpu \
  -f candidate_tag=marin-vllm-tpu-candidate-70ea9ae8f260-29548fbab663-cf8f3a6eb7e8-b5f5e06166f4 \
  -f qualification_run_id=35405315448 \
  -f promote=true
```

This dispatch reuses the accepted qualification. It must not allocate
another
TPU or rebuild the pair.

commits.author: Helw150
commits.message:
[sft] Register misconceptions and update WildChat completions (#9271)

Register `open-athena/synthetic-misconceptions-conversations` as a
structured SFT source. Every conversation in the pinned revision ends
with a user turn, so conversion removes that closing turn and retains
the preceding exchanges. All 3,450 rows then end on an assistant target,
pass chat validation, and have unique source IDs.

Advance `open-athena/wildchat-glm53-format-completions` to its 9,975-row
release. The new revision supersedes the previous 9,809-row snapshot and
retains the pinned WildChat source revision used by the existing
prompt-recovery checks.

commits.author: Helw150
commits.message:
[sft] Set explicit thinking mode for every chat conversation (#9261)

Chat normalization derives `enable_thinking` from canonical assistant
analysis messages. Conversations with at least one analysis message
enable thinking; conversations with none disable it. A conversation that
mixes analysis and non-analysis assistant turns remains in thinking
mode, and its existing messages are unchanged.

Normalization also increments
`normalize_chat/conversations_with_final_over_2k_estimated_tokens` once
per conversation when any assistant final response exceeds a
tokenizer-free estimate of 2,000 tokens. This diagnostic does not filter
records.

Bump the normalization version to `2026.09.18.1`, which invalidates
normalized, rendered, and text artifacts. Source extraction artifacts
remain reusable because source adapters continue to handle only
source-specific reasoning representations.

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grafana] Fix fork efficiency and history sampling (#9268)

Exclude inherited W&B history from a fork's progress efficiency and
projected completion calculations. The previous baseline credited parent
tokens against the child's elapsed time. The [hero
fork](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/hero-main-step121638)'s
corrected progress efficiency was about 87% when checked.

Give each displayed fork its own history sample budget in both the
training and infra report charts, while retaining the sampled parent
curve. The dashboard's 2,000-point query returned only 14 child points;
querying the child segment returned 883 points and exposed variation
hidden by the sparse tail. These fixes are separate commits.

All 34 source tests pass. The broader Grafana suite has five failures,
all reproduced on unmodified main at e07e839c34.

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[grafana] Index inference session discovery (#9269)

Restrict inference identity pickers to `num_requests_running` samples,
keeping
the selected dashboard time range while avoiding scans of unrelated
telemetry.
MarinSkyRL rows must also report `metric_source=vllm`, so non-inference
metrics
do not populate the selector.

Add an exact-name posting and a covering Finelog projection for
timestamps and
structured identity columns. During the incident, broad dashboard
queries took
6.6–8.3 seconds and pushed the one-row fleet-health probe to 7.51
seconds. The
replacement three-hour selector returned the same 42 identities in 2.89
seconds
before this projection was deployed.

The projection backfills through normal index maintenance; no producer
change
or service restart is required. See the [incident
record](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/478).

Co-authored-by: loom <claude-max-1@openathena.ai>
